root_cause: The existing 250ms watchdog limit bounded only application writer-lane acquisition. The global sqlite3.connect wrapper raises tracked connections to a 30-second SQLite busy timeout, so PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) could inherit that timeout after acquiring the lane and starve useful writers.
repair: Before acquiring the shared writer lane, the watchdog connection now sets PRAGMA busy_timeout=250. The existing 250ms writer-lane acquisition bound, TRUNCATE mode, threshold, interval, cleanup order and all normal writer settings remain unchanged.

focused_proofs.pinned_reader: A real WAL database with an open reader snapshot made TRUNCATE return SQLite BUSY in under 1 second; the writer lane was released and a subsequent writer committed normally.
focused_proofs.ordering: The SQLite busy timeout is set before application-lane acquisition.
focused_proofs.exception_cleanup: A synthetic checkpoint exception still releases the writer lane and closes the connection.
focused_proofs.tests: 79 passed across 13 relevant files, each file run in an isolated Python process to avoid the repository's known global sqlite3.connect reload contamination. The direct focused set also passed 23/23 in one process.

next_action: Prepare a module-only deployment manifest from this repair and request separate authorization before deploying src/utils/db_locking.py or restarting any service. Derive the restart set only from running services that execute the automatic WAL watchdog.
